unit.title: Communities and Maps Around the World

contentBlocks.text: This week you explored traditions and homes around the world, and practiced real map skills. Let's review it all!

Quick review: traditions vary meaningfully around the world (Day 1). Homes are shaped by local climate and materials (Day 2). Map symbols represent real things, explained by a key (Day 3). Land is usually green/brown and water is usually blue on a map (Day 4). Using a real map, find one symbol, one area of land, and one area of water, and explain what each one shows.
Wonderful work these past two weeks! You now understand that communities vary meaningfully around the world, and you have real, practical map-reading skills.

objectives: Review and connect this week's four concepts: worldwide traditions, homes and climate, map symbols, land/water
Apply map-reading skills to a real map, identifying a symbol, land, and water
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child find a symbol, land area, and water area on a real map independently.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Discuss any uncertain answers together before finishing.
5. Celebrate finishing two full weeks of Grade 1 Social Studies!
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the child to work through each of the three map tasks (symbol, land, water) as fully separate steps
Ready for more: ask them to explain how this week's map skills would help someone actually plan a trip somewhere new
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the four concepts (traditions, homes, symbols, or land/water) needs the most re-teaching
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a map-reading and review activity — check that the child can correctly identify one symbol, one land area, and one water area on a real map, and explain what each shows.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates the course's 'families and traditions around the world' and 'introduction to reading maps' descriptions before the course continues, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established across this session.

generationData.instructions: Using a real map, answer each question.

rows.problem: Find one map symbol and explain what it means.
Find one area of land and one area of water.
Why might traditions or homes look different in different parts of the world you find on the map?
